During this case management intake and planning session, the case manager (TB) met with participant **Reante Baylock** (in his 1st–2nd week with the Turn 90 program) to establish his individualized case plan, complete an intake assessment, and address immediate personal and logistical barriers.

Key highlights from the session include:

* **Personal & Family Circumstances:** Reante’s partner (a co-parent of 3 years from whom he is currently separated) is scheduled to be induced for the birth of their second child on Friday. Reante expressed significant stress regarding co-parenting friction, lack of a reliable local support network, childcare logistics for his older toddler, and financial strain (paying $150/week for daycare and supporting his children).


* **Case Plan & Focus Areas:** Reante identified **Work and Follow-Through (Card D)** and **Time and Structure (Card G)** as his primary areas for growth. They discussed coping strategies to manage anger/frustration, prevent emotional shutdowns during relationship conflicts, and structure unstructured free time to avoid past negative patterns.


* **Employment & Background:** Reante recently gave two weeks' notice at his landscaping/driving job due to scheduling conflicts with daycare drop-offs/pick-ups and lower pay ($18/hr). He previously served nearly 7 years in prison (2017/2018–2023) for drug trafficking and had an older armed robbery charge dismissed. He currently has no pending charges, probation, or formal child support/custody orders.


* **Resource Referral:** To proactively address co-parenting tension, visitation rights, and fatherhood support before legal disputes arise, TB contacted Scott at **A Father's Place (Father to Father)** and scheduled Reante for an orientation session.

### Formal Case Notes

**Participant Name:** Reante Baylock

**Case Manager:** TB (Turn 90)

**Session Type:** Case Plan Development, Intake Assessment, & Resource Referral

#### 1. Presenting Situation & Goals

* **Program Goal:** Complete the Turn 90 program and secure stable, higher-paying employment with a schedule compatible with childcare responsibilities.


* **Immediate Life Event:** Participant’s ex-partner/co-parent is scheduled for labor induction this Friday. Participant plans to attend program hours on Friday until she goes into labor, then take Monday off to support her and the newborn before returning Tuesday. Case manager advised prioritizing family needs and maintaining open communication regarding attendance.



#### 2. Case Plan Focus Areas & Action Items

Participant selected two primary focus areas from the program curriculum:

* **Focus Area 1: Work and Follow-Through (Card D / Sub-area D5 – Frustration & Loss of Motivation)**


* *Triggers Identified:* Overthinking, lack of commitment/follow-through, childcare stress, and high-conflict communication with his children's mother.


* *Selected Skills:* Skill 7 (Quitting/hopelessness/frustration-based thoughts), Skill 15 (Pausing before walking away/shutting down), and Skill 20 (Delaying emotional reactions until calm).


* *Action Items:* (1) Pause and identify feelings before disengaging; (2) Complete one challenging task without walking away or shutting down; (3) Use one self-control strategy during moments of frustration or pressure.




* **Focus Area 2: Time and Structure (Card G / Sub-area G1 – Lack of Structure & Prosocial Activities)**


* *Triggers Identified:* Excessive unstructured free time on evenings and weekends leading to boredom and negative distractions.


* *Selected Skills:* Skill 7, Skill 5, and Skill 2.


* *Action Items:* (1) Identify one prosocial activity or hobby to try; (2) Upgrade one "I don't have anything to do" boredom thought; (3) Plan weekly increases of free time in advance.





#### 3. Intake & Needs Assessment Summary

* **Documentation & Readiness:** Has valid Driver's License/ID, Birth Certificate, reliable phone, stable address (Summerville), personal vehicle/transportation, bank account, professional email, resume, 6-month job plan, and work attire. *Needs:* Social Security Card replacement.


* **Health & Wellness:** No untreated illnesses, physical limitations, or vision issues. Currently lacks health insurance/healthcare coverage and has no formal mental health/recovery support plan in place.


* **Financial & Legal:** Has reviewed credit and set savings goals, but has *not* yet completed a formal budget. Currently pays $150/week out-of-pocket for daycare. No active probation, pending charges, or formal child support/custody orders.


* **Program Progress:** Completed SkillCat intro and initial HVAC module.



#### 4. Clinical/Case Management Observations & Risk Factors

* **Emotional Regulation & Safety:** Participant reported experiencing intense anger/rage primarily triggered by co-parenting disputes (e.g., driving to West Ashley for child exchanges only to be turned away). Acknowledged that anger has led to reckless driving/speeding, representing a potential risk factor for legal/traffic infractions. Currently manages text conflicts by disengaging/swiping away messages until emotions de-escalate.


* **Support System:** Limited local support; participant’s mother occasionally babysits but cannot assist with transportation. Participant is actively looking to transfer his toddler to a more affordable daycare closer to Summerville to improve morning time management.



#### 5. Referrals & Next Steps

* **External Referral:** Case manager contacted Scott at **A Father’s Place** (North Charleston office) during the session. Scheduled participant for **Orientation on Thursday at 10:00 AM**. Participant will receive an excused pass from Turn 90 to attend orientation and subsequent Thursday classes (12:30 PM – 2:30 PM) to receive support with fatherhood skills, co-parenting, visitation/custody establishment, and financial literacy.


* **Follow-Up:** Monitor participant's attendance and family transition following Friday's birth; follow up on budget creation, Social Security card acquisition, and healthcare enrollment. | [Update 11/05/2026 • Terrence Brown]: He called Daisy and said that they induced his wife into labor which explains the sudden absence. | [Update 11/04/2026 • Terrence Brown]: NCNS 11/4/26 I called to follow up on reasons why so that we can work on a gameplan and got no answer or a call back so he was exited out of the program | [Update 11/03/2026 • Terrence Brown]: Says he couldn't make due to baby mother issues and it was his only 2nd day after starting the program

Phone Intake/Screening: Reante Baylock, 10/23/26

Background/Referral: Reante is a returning contact. He was last involved with Turn90 in 2023. I explained the current program structure: First Shift (the 8-week in-person program, 9–3, with a $450/week point-based stipend and job placement after) and Reentry Navigation (phone-based support).

Housing: He lives in an apartment with his fiancée. Housing is stable, and he doesn’t need other housing options.

Documents:

Birth certificate: yes
SS card: no
State ID: yes
Driver’s license: yes

Transportation: He has his own vehicle and will use it to get to and from the program.

Health/Behavioral Health: No prescribed medications in the last 5 years. He has no health conditions and is legally and physically able to work.

Substance Use: No history of major alcohol abuse and no drug use other than marijuana. He agreed to weekly drug testing, including THC.

Immediate Needs: None reported.

Availability: No weekly appointments or obligations conflict with the 9–3 program hours.

Criminal History:

First arrest at age 18
About 45 total arrests, 1 conviction
Most recent: released from prison 5/23/23 after 7 years. Has more recent arrests with charges that were disposed.
That conviction included drug trafficking and firearm possession
No sex offense, no pending charges
Parents have no criminal record

Supervision: None.

Child Support: None.

Education: Completed 11th grade, no GED.

Work History: Landscaping, construction, and material handling. His longest job was 2 years, and jobs usually ended due to incarceration.

Certifications: None.

Plan:

Added to the Charleston First Shift waitlist, with an estimated wait of up to about 3 weeks (could be sooner or later depending on current participants).
He declined Reentry Navigation in the meantime and prefers to wait for a spot.
I’ll update him as he moves up the waitlist. He was told he can call or text with questions.
